author: Bobby Grayson
description:
Found while writing the mapset fixture, NOT fixed (it is outside this branch's area and it fails loudly, so it is not a soundness hole).

covered_tags/3 returns a list of message tags and prepends the ATOM :all as a sentinel meaning "the bare-message clauses alone cover every state". insert_crashes/2 then asks `:all in total`. A module that declares a message tag literally named :all -- for instance @type call :: ... | :all, which is an ordinary name for "give me everything" -- makes that test true for the wrong reason. The module is then recorded as exhaustive, the global catch-all clause is suppressed, and Lean rejects the generated file with "Missing cases: ... Msg.reply ...".

Reproduce: any GenServer whose message union contains :all and whose @type reply produces an unhandled `reply` constructor. The mapset fixture had exactly that before its call was renamed from :all to :list.

The failure is always at Lean compile time, never a silently ignored message, so nothing proved is wrong. The fix is to stop using an atom that a source file can also use: have covered_tags return {tags, all_bare?} (or use a tuple sentinel), and change the two `:all in ...` tests in insert_crashes and covered_tags accordingly. Three call sites.
title: translator bug (not fixed): the :all sentinel of covered_tags collides with a message tag named :all
